title: validate-mcp-workspaces.mjs is Windows-path-dependent -- its WSL 0/20 result is invalid evidence, not real estate state
summary: Running validate-mcp-workspaces.mjs from WSL2 on CG-RYZEN9DESK-01 produces a false 0/20 result because SYNOLOGY_OPS_ROOT is hardcoded to a Windows-style path with a literal backslash. The 6 modified artifact files were reverted via git checkout -- before committing anything. Never allow a future agent to treat that WSL 0/20 result as factual estate state; it invalidates that run's evidence, not the underlying MCP surfaces.
retrievalQuestions: Why did validate-mcp-workspaces.mjs report 0 out of 20 workspaces valid when run from WSL2?
Is the WSL 0 out of 20 validate-mcp-workspaces result real evidence of a broken MCP estate?
What causes SYNOLOGY_OPS_ROOT to fail path resolution on WSL2?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A future agent runs validate-mcp-workspaces.mjs from a WSL2 host and sees a near-zero pass count
doNot: Treat a WSL2 validate-mcp-workspaces.mjs 0/20-style result as factual evidence that the MCP estate is broken
Commit artifact files modified by a run of this validator from WSL2 without first reverting them (git checkout --) if the run's own path resolution is known-broken
proveBeforeClaiming: SYNOLOGY_OPS_ROOT resolves to a real, existing path on the host the validator is actually run from before trusting its output
WC-MCP-001 (making this validator host/path-authority aware for WSL2) remains an open, not-yet-executed follow-up -- do not claim it is fixed
